title.narrative: Central African Republic (CAR) Emergency Food Crisis Response Project - Additional Financing 2

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Emergency Food Crisis Response Project for Central African Republic are to increase food production and to improve resilience of targeted smallholder farmers and food insecure households in affected areas. The project comprises of four components. The first component, support increased food production will support an accelerated supply response focused on restoring and preserving the productive capacity of farming households to enable continued and expanded production of key staple foods and livestock that is resilient to climate change. It consists of following sub-components: (i) support food production and household nutrition; (ii) support food basket distribution and linkages to market opportunities; and (iii) strengthening hydro-meteorological information for early warning. The second component, labor-intensive public works for resilience will finance livelihood support programs through labor-intensive public works (LIPW) in six prefectures and in Bangui. It consists of following sub-components: (i) rehabilitation and maintenance of small-scale agricultural infrastructures; and (ii) rehabilitation and maintenance of drainage infrastructure in Bangui. The third component, project management will finance: (i) the project day-to-day administrative, technical, and fiduciary management; (ii) the coordination of project activities across the whole scope of project execution, including management costs of specialized service providers; (iii) the establishment and implementation of a robust monitoring and evaluation (M and E) framework that relies on modern information technology (IT) and will continue as a dynamic system to support the operations of the relevant institutions beyond the project, including baseline, mid-term and final evaluation of the project; and (iv) the implementation of environmental and social (E and S) safeguard policies, citizen engagement, community mobilization measures, as well as a grievance redress mechanism (GRM). The fourth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will enable the provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.
The objectives of the project are to increase food production and to improve resilience of targeted smallholder farmers and food insecure households in affected areas.

This activity is included in WHH's contract and is set to begin before the end of December 2024

title.narrative: People living in area benefitting from improved drainage

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of people living within 1km of an improved drainage (500m on each side); calculated using a buffer area around the rehabilitated drainage and using Worldpop data to aggregate the number of people living in that area. In order to triangulate the data and refine the measurement of this indicator, the UNCT with AGETIP – CAF and the MOUS will conduct consultations (focus group) with the populations and their representatives (CDQ) to better appreciate the effects linked to the rehabilitation of the drainage system in certain districts of Bangui.

With the recent increase in beneficiaries through the 2025 input distribution campaign, these farmers are better equipped with improved seeds, fertilizers, and production support. As a result, the same group of producers is expected to experience strengthened food and nutrition security through higher yields, diversified production, and more stable household food supplies.

title.narrative: Women receiving improved nutrition services and products

comment.narrative: This indicator continues to struggle because the FAO, responsible for implementing the activity, faced significant delays in recruiting a nutrition specialist. Ultimately, they informed the client of their inability to fulfill this contractual deliverable and proposed returning the allocated budget after two years of implementation. As an alternative, the project is currently collaborating with the PUSEB's Associations of Educating Mothers to provide them with vegetable and staple crop inputs for establishing home gardens to improve children's nutrition. This activity is included in WHH's contract and is set to begin before the end of December 2024

title.narrative: Person-days of employment created for women through labor-intensive public works

comment.narrative: Person-days of employment created for women through labor-intensive public works increased from 96,114 to 132,978, representing 27% of the total 495,610 person-days generated to date and 69% of the end-of-project target of 194,000 person-days for women. This progress reflects women's growing participation in drainage system rehabilitation and maintenance works, which remain the main source of temporary employment under the project.

title.narrative: People living in area benefitting from improved drainage

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of people living within 1km of an improved drainage (500m on each side); calculated using a buffer area around the rehabilitated drainage and using Worldpop data to aggregate the number of people living in that area. In order to triangulate the data and refine the measurement of this indicator, the UNCT with AGETIP – CAF and the MOUS will conduct consultations (focus group) with the populations and their representatives (CDQ) to better appreciate the effects linked to the rehabilitation of the drainage system in certain districts of Bangui.

By the end of August 2025, 39,171 jobs had been created, including 13,524 through AGETIP, reaching 78.34% of the end-of-project target. Additional works planned by AGETIP, such as paving access roads and stabilizing riverbanks, should help achieve the target (about 9,500 jobs). This revised strategy focuses on maximizing job creation by project completion.

This revised strategy focuses on maximizing job creation by project completion.

title.narrative: Person-days of temporary employment created through labor-intensive public works

comment.narrative: The number of person-days of temporary employment created through labor-intensive public works increased from 321,090 to 495,610, reaching 73% of the end target of 680,000. This progress reflects the continued implementation of drainage system rehabilitation and maintenance works, alongside earlier achievements in the rehabilitation of 427 hectares of agricultural infrastructure by FAO. While some delays occurred due to difficulties in recruiting unskilled labor and reduced volumes of cleaning works, upcoming paving and rehabilitation activities on the Fayama and ENAM collectors are expected to close the remaining gap.

title.narrative: Grievances responded and/or resolved within the stipulated service standards for response time

comment.narrative: Since the beginning of the project, 451 complaints have been registered by the UNCT and its implementing agencies. 383 are closed (85%). 159 complaints related to the drainage works and compensation operations have been addressed to UNCT. 91 are closed (57%). This rate should be explained by the slow process of paying PAPS; a necessary activity before processing complaints.
